title: identity
aim: Explore how identity, memory, preferences and personality shape the way we describe ourselves.

Use present perfect simple and continuous accurately

lessons.title: My ID
goals: Explain how family, language and place can shape personality
Use present perfect simple and continuous for results and durations
Describe your own identity with supporting examples

grammar.title: Present perfect simple and continuous
grammar.shortAr: الماضي البسيط يركّز على النتيجة والعدد، والمستمر يركّز على النشاط ومدته.
points: Both tenses link a past situation to the present; with work, live and study the difference is often small.
Use the present perfect simple for a completed result and for How many / How much / How far questions.
Use the present perfect continuous for the activity itself, its duration with for / since, or repeated actions.
Use the simple with state verbs and with always, ever and never.
table: Result of a completed action
We've had some really interesting replies.
Activity in progress
We've been interviewing people out on the street.
How many? / How long?
I've lived in lots of places. / I've been living here for five years.
Completed vs unfinished
I've learnt that hard work pays off. / I've been learning Dutch.
State verb
How long have you known Jessica?
exceptions: State verbs take the simple, not the continuous: I've owned this car since 2009.
With live, work and study, either form is often possible.

vocab.example: She sets high goals and works hard to reach them.
He questions rules he thinks are unfair.
She asks questions about new ideas and places.
He enjoys meeting people and spending time with friends.
She smiles a lot and stays positive.
He often disagrees with other people.
She is happy to try new experiences.
He refuses to change his mind once he has decided.

practice.q: We ___ people on the street all morning; that's why we're tired.
practice.why: The activity continued over a period and explains the present tiredness.

practice.why: How many asks for a completed number, so the present perfect simple is used.

lessons.title: Memory
goals: Choose between infinitive and -ing forms after common verbs
Use memory collocations and idioms in a story

grammar.title: Infinitive and -ing forms
grammar.shortAr: بعد حروف الجر نستخدم -ing، وبعض الأفعال يتغير معناها مع to أو -ing.
points: Use an infinitive after be and to express purpose; so as (not) to is a more formal alternative.
Use an -ing form after prepositions, for example by working hard.
try, remember, forget and stop change meaning depending on whether they take an infinitive or an -ing form.
table: try to do = attempt
I tried to climb the roof, but I failed.
try doing = test a method
Try drinking green tea if your stomach hurts.
remember doing = past memory
I remember going to school for the first time.
forget to do = not do it
I forgot to feed the dog.
stop to do = pause for another action
I stopped to call my mother.
After a preposition
I passed my exams by working hard.
exceptions: After a preposition use -ing: by revising, not by to revise.
so as not to is the formal negative of an infinitive of purpose.

vocab.example: Childhood memories are things you remember from when you were very young.
My long-term memory helps me remember things for years.
Her short-term memory is good for a few moments only.
He has perfect recall for dates from his teenage years.
The smell of bread brings back memories of my grandmother.
We learned the poem by heart for the exam.
She can recall every detail of that day.

vocab.ar: يدخل من الأذن ويخرج من الأخرى

practice.why: It describes a memory of something done in the past.

practice.q: Don't forget ___ water to class tomorrow.

lessons.title: I'd much rather …
goals: Express likes, dislikes and preferences clearly
Use would rather and would prefer accurately
Compromise when planning an itinerary with others

grammar.title: Expressing personal preferences
grammar.shortAr: التفضيل: would rather + فعل بدون to، وwould prefer + to، مع عبارات للميل والكره.
points: Use phrases such as I'm really into, I'm passionate about, I'm not keen on and I'm not a big fan of with a noun or -ing form.
What I love about … is … and The thing I love about … is … focus on a particular attractive feature.
would rather takes the infinitive without to; would prefer takes the infinitive with to.
Given the choice introduces hypothetical options; I'd be happy to …, but … helps you compromise.
table: Strong like
I'm really into trying new food.
Dislike
I'm not a big fan of museums.
Focusing on a feature
What I love about this city is the street life.
Preference
I'd rather wander in a park. / I'd prefer to stay here.
Compromise
I'd be happy to visit the market, but I don't want to stay all day.
exceptions: Use -ing after prepositions: into, about and on.
I'd rather is followed by the infinitive without to, but I'd prefer takes to.

vocab.example: She is passionate about fashion and local art.
He was thrilled by the chance to explore the city.
They are fond of street markets.
I'm really into trying unusual foods.
I get nervous about getting lost in a new city.
He's terrified of the traffic in big cities.
Are you keen on visiting museums?
We were fed up of the noisy city centre.

practice.why: would rather is followed by the infinitive without to.

lessons.title: Personality
goals: Describe how personality changes in different situations
Contrast ideas with while, whereas and whilst
Write a letter of recommendation with clear examples

grammar.title: While, whereas and whilst
grammar.shortAr: while / whereas / whilst تربط فكرتين متقابلتين؛ مع بداية الجملة نضع فاصلة بعد الأولى.
points: Use while, whereas and whilst to introduce a second idea that contrasts with the first.
The linker can come at the beginning or in the middle of the sentence.
while and whilst can also introduce a time clause when two things happen at the same time.
table: Contrast at the beginning
Whilst I like Carl as a person, I wouldn't like to work for him.
Contrast in the middle
At work I'm more serious, whereas with friends I'm relaxed.
Slightly more formal
Whilst she enjoyed his company, he sometimes made her angry.
Same time
While I was stuck in bed, everyone else was enjoying the holiday.
exceptions: At the beginning, put a comma after the first clause; in the middle, put it before the linker.
while / whilst can mean during the time that, not only although.

vocab.example: She's bubbly and always laughing.
He is committed to his job and takes it seriously.
She is enthusiastic about trying new things.
He is happy-go-lucky and stays positive when things go wrong.
He gets grumpy when he is tired.
Everyone was welcoming to the new club members.
She is compassionate and cares about other people.
He is more direct at work than with friends.

video.summary: Speakers discuss personality traits and how their personalities change in different situations.

speaking: Discuss how your personality changes with friends, family, new people and at work.
Describe a partner's personality to another student and suggest a job that would suit them.
writing: Write a letter of recommendation for someone you know, describing relevant traits and giving specific examples.

practice.q: ___ I like Carl as a person, I wouldn't like to work for him.
practice.why: The sentence introduces a contrast between two ideas.

practice.q: If a contrast linker comes at the beginning, where should the comma go?
practice.why: A comma separates the first statement from the contrasting statement.

practice.q: Someone who is always laughing and full of life is ___.
practice.why: Bubbly describes a cheerful, lively personality.

practice.q: Which sentence uses while as a time clause?
options: While I was stuck in bed, everyone else was enjoying the holiday.
While I am sociable, my sister is shy.
Whereas I like tea, she prefers coffee.
practice.answer: While I was stuck in bed, everyone else was enjoying the holiday.
practice.why: It describes two things happening at the same time, not a contrast.

review.summary: Recycle identity language: present perfect forms, infinitive and -ing choices, preferences, contrast linkers and personality vocabulary.
tasks: Complete the Stormy weather anecdote with the correct forms, then check your answers with R1.
Describe three people you know using personality adjectives and contrast their traits with while or whereas.
Write a short paragraph about what shapes your identity and how you express preferences.
